head_commit.message:
Reduce redundant digamma and lgamma evaluations in special functions.

`igamma_grad_a_impl` and `random_gamma_grad_impl` evaluated both `digamma(a)` and `digamma(a + 1)` across unconditionally evaluated `select` branches even though each element only uses one branch after the loop finishes. Select `a` or `a + 1` up front and pass the shared `log(x) - digamma(...)` term into both helpers, cutting `digamma` calls from two to one in each function.

In `_hyp2f1_digamma_transform`, AMS55 15.3.10–15.3.12 only apply when `d = c - a - b` is within `50 * eps` of an integer `rd`, while a `0..|rd|` loop already runs to accumulate `log(|rd|!)`. Accumulate the harmonic sum `1 / (e - t)` inside that loop with a first-order trigamma correction for `e - |rd|`, replacing `digamma(1 + e)` and cutting `digamma` calls from three to two. Also hoist the duplicate `lax.lgamma(new_a)` call in `betaln`.

display_title: Improve accuracy of lax.digamma to within 1 ULP across all float types.

head_commit.message:
Improve accuracy of lax.digamma to within 1 ULP across all float types.

The previous CHLO lowering of `lax.digamma` (`jax.scipy.special.digamma`) loses accuracy near zeros of digamma where subtraction cancels leading digits, as well as on accelerators that flush subnormal numbers to zero or lack fused multiply-add.

Replace the CHLO lowering of `lax.digamma` for `bfloat16`, `float16`, `float32`, and `float64` with `digamma_impl` in `jax._src.lax.digamma`, keeping error within 1.0 ULP for `float64`, `float32`, and `float16` and within 0.5 ULP for `bfloat16` on CPU, GPU, and TPU. Both `float32` and `float64` shift small arguments on `[0.5, z_min)` upward with the digamma recurrence, evaluate the asymptotic Bernoulli series on larger arguments, and reflect arguments below `0.5` with Euler's reflection formula after subtracting the nearest cotangent poles at `0`, `±1`, and `±2`.

On CPU, `float32` uses native `float64` intermediates. On GPU and TPU in `float32`, and on all backends in `float64`, intermediate values are tracked as `(hi, lo)` floating-point pairs without requiring hardware FMA or subnormals, supplemented by a local Taylor polynomial around the positive zero `1.461632145` and precomputed outputs at the handful of negative inputs where cancellation exceeds working precision (three inputs in `float32` and ten in `float64`).

head_commit.message:
Test hyp1f1 over a wider domain, under strict dtype promotion

hyp1f1 relied on the implicit promotion of its bool masks to int, so it
failed under jax_numpy_dtype_promotion="strict". Build the index of the
special cases with explicit int32 casts, use typed constants in
_rgamma_and_derivative, and drop the "standard" promotion from the tests.

The precision tests now cover |a|, |b| <= 10 of either sign, down to the
smallest normal values, and all finite x. Points are only ignored for a
stated reason: results within a factor 1 / eps of overflow or underflow,
the poles of 1F1 in b, the rounding of b - a close to the poles of
gamma(b - a), cancellation between the terms hyp1f1 adds up, and the
limits of the asymptotic expansions it uses for |x| >= 100. About 19% of
the full-range random samples are now checked, instead of almost none.
float32 is checked against a float64 reference (the series, Kummer's
transformation and the asymptotic expansion, with their derivatives), and
float64 against mpmath.

This showed two issues in the series, fixed here: they could stop after a
first negligible term although later terms grow (a close to 0 or to a
negative integer, or b close to a pole), and their first term could
underflow once scaled by exp(x / 2).

head_commit.message:
Fall back to caller location for bare-NameLoc MLIR callsites in source_mapper.

In modern Pallas and Mosaic MLIR debug dumps (such as `pltpu.emit_pipeline`), callsite locations frequently have a bare `NameLoc` or scoped `NameLoc` callee with no `FileLineColLoc`, while the caller location carries the originating Python source line. Previously, `parse_mlir_locations` treated callsites as unconditional redirects to the callee ID, raising `KeyError` whenever a bare `NameLoc` was absent from `locations`.

Record both `callee` and `caller` on `Callsite` entries and resolve locations recursively with cycle detection, preferring `callee` when it resolves to a `Location` and falling back to `caller` otherwise. Unresolved bare `NameLoc` entries without file locations are skipped cleanly.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Lower log and log1p to YNNPACK SIMD bitcode kernels

Replaces the XLA:CPU implementations of `log` and `log1p` in the MLIR fusion
pipeline with YNNPACK SIMD kernels compiled to LLVM bitcode via `cc_to_llvm_ir`:

- Compile YNNPACK SIMD `log` and `log1p` kernels for 128-bit, 256-bit (AVX2),
  and 512-bit (AVX-512) vector targets into embedded LLVM bitcode.
- Support single-precision (`f32`, `v2f32`, `v4f32`, `v8f32`, `v16f32`) and
  double-precision (`f64`, `v2f64`, `v4f64`, `v8f64`) types.
- F16 and BF16 continue to upcast to F32 via the existing
  `LowerXlaIntrinsicLibPass` infrastructure.
- Preserve signed zero for `log1p(-0.0) = -0.0` via `copysign`.
- Upcast F16/BF16 `log1p` to F32 in the CPU elemental emitter (used for small
  while loops), since the YNNPACK `log1p` kernels have no F16 variant.
- Windows (where bitcode embedding is disabled) and GPU continue to use `libm`
  and handwritten `log1p` lowering.
- Relax the JAX CPU float64 `log` accuracy bound (and `docs/accuracy.md`) to
  1.5 ULP, matching NVIDIA GPU; it previously assumed a correctly rounded
  `libm` `log`.
- Tighten the JAX CPU float32 `log1p` bound from 3.0 to 2.5 ULP (exhaustive max
  2.16 ULP).
- Relax tolerances in TF tests that compare XLA against `numpy` at 1-2 ULP:
  float64 `geomspace` in `np_test` (to `1e-14`, as for `complex128`) and
  float32 `Log1pTest` on CPU (to `2.5e-7`, as on GPU).
- Remove `GenerateVF32Log` from `polynomial_approximations.cc` while retaining
  `GenerateVF32Exp`.

to a supported target (`vmem` or `hbm`).

Fixes #41844

display_title: Support reverse-mode autodiff for generic lax.reduce_window

head_commit.message:
Support reverse-mode autodiff for generic lax.reduce_window

The JVP of a generic reduce_window (a custom computation, not
add/max/min) produced its primal and tangent outputs from a single
reduce_window_p over (primal, tangent) pairs. That cannot be partially
evaluated or transposed, so jax.grad failed with "Linearization failed
to produce known values for all output primals" (#7815). It also passed
symbolic-zero operand tangents straight through, which broke
differentiation of variadic reduce_windows with a constant operand, for
example the indices of a windowed argmax (#32548).

The JVP now evaluates the reduction as a fold over the window offsets:
each output starts at its init value and absorbs one strided slice of
the padded operand per window offset, in row-major order, with padding
and base-dilation holes masked out. This matches how XLA evaluates
reduce_window, including for non-associative computations, and is built
only from primitives with transpose rules, so reverse mode works.
Operand tangents that are symbolic zeros are instantiated first.

Fixes #7815 (generic path) and #32548.

display_title: [Pallas:MGPU] Support transposing the swizzled dimension in `UnswizzleRef`.

head_commit.message:
[Pallas:MGPU] Support transposing the swizzled dimension in `UnswizzleRef`.

Previously, `UnswizzleRef` assumed the swizzled dimension was always the minormost dimension (`-1`) and rejected any `TransposeTransform` that moved it. Because of this restriction, `_get_lowering_rule` and `_swap_lowering_rule` had to manually pop `UnswizzleRef` before calling `_handle_transforms`: when a tiled and swizzled SMEM reference is transposed, commuting `TransposeTransform` past `UntilingTransform` also transposes the 2D tile dimensions, which moves the swizzled dimension away from `-1`.

To allow `UnswizzleRef` to flow through `_handle_transforms` uniformly with `UntilingTransform` (in a followup change), `UnswizzleRef` needs to track which dimension is swizzled (`swizzled_dim`) across `TransposeTransform` and `NDIndexer` rather than assuming it is always `-1`, while enforcing that operations requiring the swizzled dimension to remain minormost (`undo` and `commute_reshape`) or un-sliced (`commute_ndindexer`) check `swizzled_dim`.

display_title: [jax] Rescale cg right-hand side by a power of two to avoid inner-product underflow and overflow

head_commit.message:
[jax] Rescale cg right-hand side by a power of two to avoid inner-product underflow and overflow

When `jax.scipy.sparse.linalg.cg` is called with a small right-hand side, such as the incoming cotangent in reverse-mode automatic differentiation when a downstream loss has a small scale, quadratic inner products in `_cg_solve` can underflow in float32 or float16. With a preconditioner `M` that shrinks the residual, the preconditioned inner product `gamma` can underflow to exact zero while the unpreconditioned residual norm squared remains positive, causing the next iteration to divide zero by zero and return all-NaN outputs. Conversely, a very large right-hand side overflows the initial norm squared to infinity and causes `cg` to exit immediately with the initial guess.

Rescale the right-hand side, initial guess, and absolute tolerance in `_cg_solve` by the power-of-two exponent of the maximum absolute entry of `(b, x0)`, undo the scaling on the converged solution with `ldexp`, stop iterating if `gamma` or `p^H A p` underflows to zero, and use a zero initial guess for the transpose solve in `_isolve`. Because scaling by a power of two is exact in IEEE floating-point arithmetic and conjugate gradient is homogeneous in the right-hand side, initial guess, and absolute tolerance, normal-range solves remain bitwise identical while extreme magnitudes no longer underflow or overflow.

Fixes #40254.

display_title: [jax] Rescale cg right-hand side by a power of two to avoid inner-product underflow and overflow

head_commit.message:
[jax] Rescale cg right-hand side by a power of two to avoid inner-product underflow and overflow

When `jax.scipy.sparse.linalg.cg` is called with a small right-hand side, such as the incoming cotangent in reverse-mode automatic differentiation when a downstream loss has a small scale, quadratic inner products in `_cg_solve` can underflow in float32 or float16. With a preconditioner `M` that shrinks the residual, the preconditioned inner product `gamma` can underflow to exact zero while the unpreconditioned residual norm squared remains positive, causing the next iteration to divide zero by zero and return all-NaN outputs. Conversely, a very large right-hand side overflows the initial norm squared to infinity and causes `cg` to exit immediately with the initial guess.

Rescale the right-hand side, initial guess, and absolute tolerance in `_cg_solve` by the power-of-two exponent of the maximum absolute entry of `(b, x0)`, undo the scaling on the converged solution with `ldexp`, stop iterating if `gamma` underflows to zero, and use a zero initial guess for the transpose solve in `_isolve`. Because scaling by a power of two is exact in IEEE floating-point arithmetic and conjugate gradient is homogeneous in the right-hand side, initial guess, and absolute tolerance, normal-range solves remain bitwise identical while extreme magnitudes no longer underflow or overflow.

Fixes #40254.

head_commit.message:
Fall back to caller location for bare-NameLoc MLIR callsites in source_mapper.

In modern Pallas and Mosaic MLIR debug dumps (such as `pltpu.emit_pipeline`), callsite locations frequently have a bare `NameLoc` or scoped `NameLoc` callee with no `FileLineColLoc`, while the caller location carries the originating Python source line. Previously, `parse_mlir_locations` treated callsites as unconditional redirects to the callee ID, raising `KeyError` whenever a bare `NameLoc` was absent from `locations`.

Record both `callee` and `caller` on `Callsite` entries and resolve locations recursively with cycle detection, preferring `callee` when it resolves to a `Location` and falling back to `caller` otherwise. Unresolved bare `NameLoc` entries without file locations are skipped cleanly.

head_commit.message:
[JAX] Fix jax.scipy.linalg.toeplitz (and hankel) NaN propagation

Problem:
In https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38636 (and https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/38635), `jax.scipy.linalg.toeplitz` and `jax.scipy.linalg.hankel` propagated NaNs incorrectly because their underlying implementations used `lax.conv_general_dilated_patches`. This convolution implementation expands `NaN` pollution across the entire output matrix due to structural zero padding interacting with `NaN`.

Solution:
